Immunotherapy: The living trials

By: Sasha Schwendenwein | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Imagine you didn't need harmful chemotherapy or radiation, and a death sentence could be lifted by having your own immune system killing the cancer? Well that's immunotherapy and the trials are over.

Unique Selling Point:
There are traditionally 4 ways to treat cancer,
1. Chemotherapy
2. Radiation
3. Surgery
4. Targeted therapy (developed about 10-11 years ago – found that a certain type of cancer has a mutation – cancer cell’s contain DNA – some cancer like lung and melanoma- has a break which is called a mutation – one single mutation is abnormal – develop a drug that inhibits the abnormality… - almost 100% effective…. A patient on oxygen and then a few days later will be walking around – so amazing – BUT IT doesn’t last forever. Works quickly, but as cancer mutates quickly it comes back after 2-3 years this treatment will fail and return.

THEN THERE IS 5. Immunotherapy – The Nobel Prize for Medicine or Physiology 2018 was awarded to James P. Allison of the University of Texas MD Anderson Cancer Center and Tasuku Honjo of Kyoto University for their discovery of cancer therapy by inhibition of negative immune regulation.- i.e. Immunotherapy. It is life changing - and its as simple as going in for a drip for 30 minutes every 3 weeks. Immunotherapy uses your your body's on immune system to recognize the cancer cells and kill them. Basically - put simply cancer forms when your cells do not die - apotosis (cell death) is inhibited.

In 2018 two kinds of medicine that these doctors created was trialed in South Africa - and its taken 2 years but not Dr Sze Wai Chan who has headed the trials is giving us exclusive access to meet those patients who should have died.

Trials are very interesting in that they usually are comprise of patients who are diagnosed with stage 4 first - this means that doctors have looked at their cancer and concluded they cannot recover from it. But Dr Chan, has tested both medicines to astonishing results.


Summary:
10 years ago you didn’t meet a melanoma survivor, but when this drug came along, it stimulates a specific pathway in the patient - teaches immune system how to activate its immune system, and it corrects the pathway - only works in 20% of melanoma patients, what is surprising is that they don’t die – 10-15 years – so they had a sustained response… as it has now taught your immune system to fight it naturally.

Its simple and quick many patients come in on their lunch breaks and don't have to tell ppl they have stage 4 cancer. Also it doesn't make them feel bad at all - no side effects!



Further information:
There are two kinds of drugs: Pembrolizumab /petruder – newer generation drug – developed about 5 years ago, what this drugs does it perfect the immune teaching, it has less side effects… must safer, you have an increase in response rate – 40% patients survive – this response is sustained.

And Antipd1… which is a check point inhibitor. Cancer it blocks the gateway of the cancer cell being able to enter a health cell and mutate. Basically the cancer cant grows and your immune system kills it, they dont have hair loss, they aren't tired.

Dr Chan is unlike any other doctor ive met. Her mannerisms and bed side way are so welcoming and friendly and warm. She says she considers her patients her friends - unlike most doctors she is very personal with her patients. She will hand draw how the medicines work, and will give us access to trial clinic - show us how it works and will give us personal time with her in her office seeing what her life is like.

Regarding the cost of immunotherapy in private practice - let's just stick to pembrolizumab as an example for melanoma.

Discovery will only pay for Classic comprehensive or higher plans, and pays only 75% towards the cost, and the patient need to pay 25% co-payment. At this time, the price of pembrolizumab is R82,000 per treatment. The treatment is once every 3 weeks for up to 2 years (if the patient is responding).

Other medical aid may or may not pay depending on which ones. Profmed, bankmed, camaf will pay, with similar co-payments "punishing" the patients.

If the patient is successfully enrolled onto a clinical trial with immunotherapy, then the patient does not need to pay anything, as the drugs and procedures (blood tests, scans, etc) are paid for by the trials / sponsor company.

Extra Budget Items:
We have 3 patients who were given death sentences. We are going to go to their houses and see them living - a normal life. Very nice personal story.

Mr Graham Hayes said yes. He has stage IV melanoma in 2019 and was enrolled onto a clinical trial with immunotherapy. The cancer has largely disappeared. He is well on treatment and lives a normal active life. He also does crazy amount of sports and still looks amazing at the age of 69.


Anne Schmidt. She cannot wait to talk about her own experience on immunotherapy clinical trial. She is amazing. Stage IV lung cancer, extremely short of breath around christmas 2019. Enrolled her on an immunotherapy clinical trial and she is on 2 different immunotherapy agents. Responded quickly and cancer has almost disappeared. She would have died in 3 months if she did not receive this treatment.

Mr Philip Brotherton is happy to be interviewed. He is a lovely and interesting man. He runs a bodyguard/security business called Ipeleng (ipeleng.co.za) - He has stage IV renal pelvis cancer (cancer in the "tubes" next to the kidney). Gone through chemo before, but relapsed, then went onto immunotherapy since August 2019. Complete response on immunotherapy and is still on treatment. He knows the difference between chemo vs immuno regarding side effects and efficacy.


I EVEN HAVE A BACK UP: Mr Bradley McCann is happy to be on Carte Blanche - 0836321933.

Stage IV melanoma in 2018, spread to the lung and has other spreading to skin and small bowel. He was initially told to have the lung metastasis cut out (by a surgeon).

Came to see me, no surgery was done and started pembrolizumab. Had 2 full years of treatment (paid for by his medical aid). Complete response - no cancer seen. Hardly any side effects - only has a little bit of itchy nose and eyes. The immunotherapy has help him avoid unnecessary lung surgery (which is a big op) and also give him a normal life with excellent control - possibly a cure.

Guy Cronje the rugby guy said YES to Carte Blanche. Please contact him - guy.cronje@gmail.com or 0829239278. I think he is based in Durban. Maybe you can film him playing rugby.

He was 26 when he was diagnosed with stage III melanoma (2015). Lucky for him, he was enrolled onto one of the earliest melanoma immunotherapy trial called CHECKMATE 238. He had 2 years of treatment and is still disease free. These treatments were not even available commercially at that time.

Script:


In 2007 Dr Sze Wei Chan was a fledgling doctor training to become an oncologist.
Chan: When I just became a doctor, I came across cancer patients and during one of the rotations of the cancer training, I just felt like, you know, this is amazing because the science has been improving so much.
She now heads up all cancer trials at Sandton’s Oncology Centre using that scientific advancement to save terminal cancer patients' lives.
TRADITIONALLY THERE WERE 4 TYPES OF CANCER TREATMENT: CHEMOTHERAPY, RADIATION, SURGERY AND TARGETED THERAPY – BUT THEN CAME ALONG IMMUNOTHERAPY. DISCOVERED BY TWO DOCTORS WHO WON THE NOBEL PRIZE FOR MEDICINE IN 2018, ITS A LIFE CHANGING TREATMENT - AND ITS AS SIMPLE AS GOING IN FOR A DRIP FOR 30 MINUTES EVERY 3 WEEKS.
Chan: So the traditional treatment of cancer usually consists trying to create a drug that kills the cancer directly. But cancer is always very clever. It will always bypass the pressure And that's how we get recurrence. Now with immunotherapy, we are merely using a drug to correct our own immune system in order for our immune system to go and kill the cancer ourselves.
Dr Chan has 359 patients currently enrolled in 27 global trials consisting of various kinds of cancer.
So the earliest trial is on a petri dish, and then if there's any interaction between the drug and the cancer and that shows promises, then we will enter into what we call a phase one trial in order to find a safe dose to be given to human beings. Then we will move onto the phase two trials, and what we needed to find out is whether there's any efficacy in a real world setting. then we move on to what we call a Phase three trial. Now the control group usually is consisting of the standard of care, meaning that the current standard of care, so, for example, in lung cancer, it has been chemotherapy. So the control group would be chemotherapy and a placebo.so that's how we compare whether the trial drug would exert a better survival benefit than the control arm.
IN 2016 CARTE BLANCHE REPORTED ON THE FIRST IMMUNOTHERAPY DRUG TRIALS, BUT NOW ITS BETTER, SAFER AND LESS EXPENSIVE.
since then we have developed another drug, which is called Pembrolizumab Now what usually happens is the immune cells can go and recognize the cancer, and go directly and kill the cancer, however the cancer is very clever and created a block between the cancer and immune cells, what we needed to do was create an antibody, and this basically breaks the bond.
10 YEARS AGO, YOU DIDN’T MEET A MELANOMA SURVIVOR, BUT THEN IMMUNOTHERAPY CAME ALONG, AND GRAHAM HAYES WHO HAD STAGE 4 MELANOMA IN 2019 WAS GIVEN A NEW LEASE ON LIFE AT 69 YEARS OLD.
Hayes: I developed a lump on the side of my neck, the primary lesion here was a two and a half centimeters in size.
His illness coincided with the beginning of Dr Chan’s Pembrolizumab drug trial.
Hayes: they were seeing something like 60 percent successful results. So from our point of view, it was a no brainer, except the cost because it's metastatic, you need 34 treatments. So that's three point four million rand,. we then discovered that discovery will pay up to 75 percent of that. Then she said, I'm running a trial on behalf of the drug manufacturers and you are a perfect candidate.
And trials are free. Although expensive, the prices have decreased from R250,000 per treatment, and are cheaper than other countries like America.
Chan: It costs approximately eighty two thousand rand every three weeks. OK, so you can imagine that is really not affordable at all. However, most of the major medical aids do support the patients, but only on a higher tier of the medical aid.
Hayes had few side effects.
This was the most extraordinary thing, my lifestyle hadn't changed from the time that I heard the news to the time to where I've now got to where I'm cancer free.
And immunotherapy patients remain cancer free.
DOCTORS ALWAYS TRIAL STAGE 4 PATIENTS FIRST TO SEE THE EFFICACY IN SOMEONE WHO WAS TOLD THE DISEASE WILL KILL HEM. ANNE SCHMIDT WAS EXTREMELY SHORT OF BREATH, ONLY TO FIND OUT SHE HAD STAGE 4 LUNG CANCER AROUND CHRISTMAS 2019 – SHE WAS GIVEN 3 MONTHS TO LIVE.
AS: It's a feeling out of breath th at was wheezing and started to cough again, I had already had one lung removed
Schmidt decided instead of surgery and chemotherapy, this time she wouldn’t fight it.
You don't want to eat certain territories on your plate and you know, you just want to curl up in a little ball...
But then Dr Chan offered her a spot on the trial.
A: I thought they can learn something from this immunotherapy ill go for it.
C: So your motivation actually for going on immunotherapy was for the scientists and the doctors to learn?
A I didnt think Id get better, and slowly but surely, the tumors started decreasing.
C: So where are we now?
A: My doctor just said to me if they didn't know what they were looking for when they did the last scan, they wouldn't see anything. And I was astounded. As I said, I've got hold of hospice after the whole death scene and then I didn't die.
C: Hospice plans are best plans to be cancelled!
A: I live to fight another day!
SOME CANCER PATIENTS HAVE HAD OTHER FORMS OF TREATMENT BEFORE THEY BECAME PART OF AN IMMUNOTHERAPY TRIAL. PHILIP BROTHERTON HAS STAGE 4 RENAL PELVIS CANCER EXPLAINS THE DIFFERENCE BETWEEN THE SIDE EFFECTS AND EFFICACY OF BOTH CHEMOTHERAPY AND IMMUNOTHERAPY.
Philip: I was booked in the day before christmas…Because we all we've all getting chemo. Yes, we all got cancer. And when you look around. You're not doing too bad when you look at some of the people and you're feeling sorry for yourself. It doesn't matter. you've got to make your mind up whether you're going to be positive or negative because the negative will kill you.
Dr Chan then switched him to immunotherapy which
Bortherton decided was worth the cost.
P: I found God during this whole ordeal. And. I'm cancer free. I'm actually a miracle.
C:What would you say to those like you a bit sceptical about immunotherapy?
A: Catch a wake up, if it abash, I mean, dont stop fighting, fight!
Hayes says Dr Chan really bonds with her patients.
Hayes: what we did discover at the time is that she does have a dry sense of humor, because every time I see I have another mark, my body would had fallen off my back and it just she'd look up and said, you're not very good, are you?
South Africans are now able to check where trials are available through this website.
Chan: “It’s called clinicaltrials.gov…. so for example i wanted to look for a melanoma trial and… click search, and then it will give you all the recruiting studies at this moment.”
Chan: Yeah, so I don't think we can get rid of chemotherapy or radiotherapy or any other traditional treatment yet, so 50 percent of the patients will respond, so we needed to understand why the other 50 percent of patients do not respond to immunotherapy.

Chan: “It’s called clinicaltrials.gov…. so for example i wanted to look for a melanoma trial and… click search, and then it will give you all the recruiting studies at this moment.” Chan: Yeah, so I don't think we can get rid of chemotherapy or radiotherapy or any other traditional treatment yet, so 50 percent of the patients will respond, so we needed to understand why the other 50 percent of patients do not respond to immunotherapy.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Imagine you didn't need harmful chemotherapy or radiation, and a death sentence could be lifted by having your own immune system killing the cancer? Well that's immunotherapy and the trials are over.
metadata.Unique Selling Point: There are traditionally 4 ways to treat cancer, 1. Chemotherapy 2. Radiation 3. Surgery 4. Targeted therapy (developed about 10-11 years ago – found that a certain type of cancer has a mutation – cancer cell’s contain DNA – some cancer like lung and melanoma- has a break which is called a mutation – one single mutation is abnormal – develop a drug that inhibits the abnormality… - almost 100% effective…. A patient on oxygen and then a few days later will be walking around – so amazing – BUT IT doesn’t last forever. Works quickly, but as cancer mutates quickly it comes back after 2-3 years this treatment will fail and return. THEN THERE IS 5. Immunotherapy – The Nobel Prize for Medicine or Physiology 2018 was awarded to James P. Allison of the University of Texas MD Anderson Cancer Center and Tasuku Honjo of Kyoto University for their discovery of cancer therapy by inhibition of negative immune regulation.- i.e. Immunotherapy. It is life changing - and its as simple as going in for a drip for 30 minutes every 3 weeks. Immunotherapy uses your your body's on immune system to recognize the cancer cells and kill them. Basically - put simply cancer forms when your cells do not die - apotosis (cell death) is inhibited. In 2018 two kinds of medicine that these doctors created was trialed in South Africa - and its taken 2 years but not Dr Sze Wai Chan who has headed the trials is giving us exclusive access to meet those patients who should have died. Trials are very interesting in that they usually are comprise of patients who are diagnosed with stage 4 first - this means that doctors have looked at their cancer and concluded they cannot recover from it. But Dr Chan, has tested both medicines to astonishing results.
metadata.Summary: 10 years ago you didn’t meet a melanoma survivor, but when this drug came along, it stimulates a specific pathway in the patient - teaches immune system how to activate its immune system, and it corrects the pathway - only works in 20% of melanoma patients, what is surprising is that they don’t die – 10-15 years – so they had a sustained response… as it has now taught your immune system to fight it naturally. Its simple and quick many patients come in on their lunch breaks and don't have to tell ppl they have stage 4 cancer. Also it doesn't make them feel bad at all - no side effects!
metadata.Further information: There are two kinds of drugs: Pembrolizumab /petruder – newer generation drug – developed about 5 years ago, what this drugs does it perfect the immune teaching, it has less side effects… must safer, you have an increase in response rate – 40% patients survive – this response is sustained. And Antipd1… which is a check point inhibitor. Cancer it blocks the gateway of the cancer cell being able to enter a health cell and mutate. Basically the cancer cant grows and your immune system kills it, they dont have hair loss, they aren't tired. Dr Chan is unlike any other doctor ive met. Her mannerisms and bed side way are so welcoming and friendly and warm. She says she considers her patients her friends - unlike most doctors she is very personal with her patients. She will hand draw how the medicines work, and will give us access to trial clinic - show us how it works and will give us personal time with her in her office seeing what her life is like. Regarding the cost of immunotherapy in private practice - let's just stick to pembrolizumab as an example for melanoma. Discovery will only pay for Classic comprehensive or higher plans, and pays only 75% towards the cost, and the patient need to pay 25% co-payment. At this time, the price of pembrolizumab is R82,000 per treatment. The treatment is once every 3 weeks for up to 2 years (if the patient is responding). Other medical aid may or may not pay depending on which ones. Profmed, bankmed, camaf will pay, with similar co-payments "punishing" the patients. If the patient is successfully enrolled onto a clinical trial with immunotherapy, then the patient does not need to pay anything, as the drugs and procedures (blood tests, scans, etc) are paid for by the trials / sponsor company.
metadata.Extra Budget Items: We have 3 patients who were given death sentences. We are going to go to their houses and see them living - a normal life. Very nice personal story. Mr Graham Hayes said yes. He has stage IV melanoma in 2019 and was enrolled onto a clinical trial with immunotherapy. The cancer has largely disappeared. He is well on treatment and lives a normal active life. He also does crazy amount of sports and still looks amazing at the age of 69. Anne Schmidt. She cannot wait to talk about her own experience on immunotherapy clinical trial. She is amazing. Stage IV lung cancer, extremely short of breath around christmas 2019. Enrolled her on an immunotherapy clinical trial and she is on 2 different immunotherapy agents. Responded quickly and cancer has almost disappeared. She would have died in 3 months if she did not receive this treatment. Mr Philip Brotherton is happy to be interviewed. He is a lovely and interesting man. He runs a bodyguard/security business called Ipeleng (ipeleng.co.za) - He has stage IV renal pelvis cancer (cancer in the "tubes" next to the kidney). Gone through chemo before, but relapsed, then went onto immunotherapy since August 2019. Complete response on immunotherapy and is still on treatment. He knows the difference between chemo vs immuno regarding side effects and efficacy. I EVEN HAVE A BACK UP: Mr Bradley McCann is happy to be on Carte Blanche - 0836321933. Stage IV melanoma in 2018, spread to the lung and has other spreading to skin and small bowel. He was initially told to have the lung metastasis cut out (by a surgeon). Came to see me, no surgery was done and started pembrolizumab. Had 2 full years of treatment (paid for by his medical aid). Complete response - no cancer seen. Hardly any side effects - only has a little bit of itchy nose and eyes. The immunotherapy has help him avoid unnecessary lung surgery (which is a big op) and also give him a normal life with excellent control - possibly a cure. Guy Cronje the rugby guy said YES to Carte Blanche. Please contact him - guy.cronje@gmail.com or 0829239278. I think he is based in Durban. Maybe you can film him playing rugby. He was 26 when he was diagnosed with stage III melanoma (2015). Lucky for him, he was enrolled onto one of the earliest melanoma immunotherapy trial called CHECKMATE 238. He had 2 years of treatment and is still disease free. These treatments were not even available commercially at that time.
